# Acts of Thomas — Chapter 4
**Agent:** PNEUMA (Dynamic)
**Source:** Syriac MS / Greek recension, Acts of Thomas 4

---

*[THE PALACE REVEALED. Dead men and heavenly real estate.]*

1. The king came back from his travels and started asking around: where's my palace?

2. "There is no palace," his friends said. "He gave everything away to the poor. He says he built you a palace in heaven."

3. The king exploded with rage. He had Thomas and Abbanes seized and thrown in prison. He started planning what kind of death Thomas should die.

4. They sat in prison.

5. But then — the king's brother Gad fell ill and died.

6. The king was devastated. He loved his brother deeply.

7. When Gad's body was being laid out, angels took his soul and carried it up to heaven. They showed him the dwelling-places there, room after room.

8. And then he saw it: a palace of extraordinary beauty. He wanted to live there immediately.

9. "This palace," the angels told him, "belongs to your brother. The Christian he imprisoned — this is what that man built for him."

10. Gad said: "Please — let me go back. Let me go back and buy it from my brother. He doesn't know what he has. He'll sell it."

11. They let him go. He came back to life.

12. When he opened his eyes, his brother was sitting right beside his body, keeping watch.

13. "Brother," Gad said, "that slave you put in prison — give him to me. I need to buy something from him."

14. "What could he possibly have to sell?" the king said.

15. "Bring him here," Gad said. "And I'll tell you what I saw."

16. The king was shaken. He ordered Thomas released from prison.

17. When Thomas came in, Gad threw himself at his feet. "Please," he said. "Sell me the upper chamber of the palace you built in heaven. I want it. I need it."

18. Thomas said: "I can't. That room belongs to your brother. I built it for him."

19. "Then sell it to me."

20. "I can't sell what isn't mine to sell," Thomas said. "But your brother can give it to you, if he chooses."

21. In that moment, the king understood everything. He believed. He and his brother Gad were both baptized.

---
*PNEUMA note: The passage from death to life to heavenly negotiation to conversion happens in minutes of narrative time. Gad's desire to purchase the upper chamber is not comic — it is a man who has glimpsed glory and cannot bear to lose it. The king's conversion is total and immediate: understanding brings faith.*
